title: The abolition of the net metering scheme is final: how can you get the most out of your panels?
excerpt: The abolition of the net metering scheme is final: How can you still get the most out of your panels?
contentHtml:
Yesterday, the Dutch Senate made an important decision: the net metering scheme for solar panel owners will be abolished from 2027. This means that households with solar panels will no longer be able to offset their electricity consumption with the solar energy they feed back into the grid. Although the political debate on net metering has been going on for some time, it will mean a significant change for many solar panel owners. What exactly does this entail? And how can you make smart use of your solar energy in the future? We explain.

What exactly is the net metering scheme?

Often, the solar panels on your roof generate more electricity during the day than you consume at that moment. The surplus solar energy is then fed back into the electricity grid. The net metering scheme offers the possibility to deduct this fed-back energy from your annual consumption, as it were. This results in a lower energy bill.

The net metering scheme has been extremely beneficial for solar panel owners. Offsetting their energy consumption against their energy generation made investing in solar panels very attractive financially. However, with an increasingly congested electricity grid and declining tax revenues, the question was how long this system would remain sustainable.

What will change from 2027 onwards?

The net metering scheme will be completely phased out, meaning that from January 1, 2027, solar panel owners will no longer be allowed to net meter. This means that the electricity you feed back into the grid can no longer be deducted from (or offset against) the electricity you consume. Instead, from 2027 onwards, you will only receive compensation for the energy you feed back into the grid. Until January 1, 2030, this so-called feed-in tariff will be set at a minimum of 50 percent of the basic supply price, which is considerably lower than the current benefit. In short: feeding solar energy back into the grid will become less advantageous.

In addition, energy suppliers introduced feed-in costs last year. The House of Representatives wanted to ban feed-in costs, which has been partially implemented. From 2027, these feed-in costs may no longer be linked to the net metering scheme. However, feed-in costs may still be charged for so-called imbalance costs. Although the feed-in costs will be lower, they will not disappear completely. All in all, the abolition of the net metering scheme means that feed-in will become less attractive from 2027 onwards, both because of lower payments and possible additional costs.

Making better use of solar energy is becoming important

The abolition of the net metering scheme means that it will become less financially attractive to feed your surplus solar energy back into the grid. From 2027 onwards, it will therefore be essential to use the electricity you generate yourself more intelligently. It is a shame if your solar panels produce a lot of energy during the day, while you do not use that energy immediately. This means you benefit less from your investment in solar panels.

The solution? Increase your own consumption, also known as self-use. The more of your self-generated energy you use directly, the less you depend on the grid and the associated costs, and the more you benefit from your solar panels.

How can you still get the most out of your solar panels?

A simple and affordable way to do this is to use the WaterAccu. This smart technology makes it possible to store excess solar energy in the form of hot water. This allows you to use your energy immediately, for example to heat your shower water.

With the WaterAccu, you can get the most out of your solar panels and prevent your investment from losing value after 2027. By using your own energy efficiently, you can reduce your energy costs and make yourself less dependent on the net metering scheme, feed-in tariffs, and fluctuations in energy prices. In short, self-consumption is the future for solar panel owners – and the WaterAccu helps you do this in a smart and cost-effective way.
